text:
The week was a strong rally for Indian equities. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,030.35, up 2.01% on the day and 8.58% for the week, while Bank Nifty rose 2.27% daily and 8.04% weekly. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) kept buying for an eighth straight session, netting INR 45,960 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) stayed net sellers with INR ‑24,196 crore. Breadth was healthy – 217 advancers versus 271 decliners, and 71.2% of stocks stayed above their 20‑day moving average.

Among IPOs, the most recent listings were BLS Polymers (issue price ₹150, listing gain 65.3%) and SFC Environmental Technologies (issue price ₹330, gain 7.6%). Both opened in late‑October and listed early November. No new IPOs are open or scheduled for the coming week according to the data, so the market will watch any fresh filings that may appear.

Key drivers for next week include the continued inflow of foreign capital, a still‑elevated India VIX at 17.47 (a measure of market volatility), and external cues: the USD‑INR slipped 0.66% over five days to 93.89, Brent crude fell 0.64% and gold slipped 1.36%. Global equity futures showed mixed signals – S&P 500 up 0.8% but Nasdaq down 2.01%. These macro trends, together with sector‑quadrant shifts (financial services, consumption and infrastructure leading, while IT and pharma weaken), could shape market direction.
